title: Anti-Corruption After The Plenum
gist: Gavekal argues China's anti-corruption drive, still processing tens of thousands of cases monthly in 2026, has become a system of political supervision aimed at enforcing top-down compliance with central directives. The Fifth Plenum, devoted to Party self-governance, confirmed this by integrating conduct improvement and discipline enforcement with anti-corruption measures.

insights.claim: The CCDI is still processing tens of thousands of cases every month in 2026, including high-ranking current and former officials, signalling that the campaign's intensity has not faded and no one is exempt.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Elite-level risk of purges remains a persistent feature of Chinese politics, not a past-cycle event.
insights.quote: The Central Commission for Discipline Inspection is still churning through tens of thousands of cases every month
insights.locator: 2026 has been another extraordinarily busy year

insights.claim: The campaign's purpose goes beyond rooting out financial impropriety to building a system for enforcing compliance with central directives, which Xi sees as a widespread problem.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Policy announcements from Beijing are likely to be backed by disciplinary enforcement, raising odds of local implementation.
insights.quote: building a system for enforcing compliance with central directives, which top leader Xi Jinping sees as a widespread problem
insights.locator: All this effort is aimed not only at

insights.claim: Xi's central concern is effective top-down transmission of orders, implying that local-level non-implementation and say-one-thing-do-another behaviour is the governance failure he is trying to fix.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Local official caution or foot-dragging is treated as a political offence, which may push officials toward over-compliance or inaction out of fear.
insights.quote: The most important issue for Xi is the effective top-down transmission of orders.
insights.locator: The most important issue for Xi

insights.claim: The Fifth Plenum, concluded on Thursday 29 Oct 2026, was devoted to 'advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance', i.e. how the Party selects, manages and disciplines officials, rather than an economic agenda.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Read the plenum as an organisational and political-control signal; do not expect headline economic stimulus from it.
insights.quote: advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance
insights.locator: He has devoted the Party's Fifth Plenum

insights.claim: The plenum confirmed that anti-corruption has already largely been transformed into a system of political supervision, agreeing to integrate conduct improvement and discipline enforcement with anti-corruption measures.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Institutionalisation means the campaign is likely permanent infrastructure, lowering the chance of a relaxation phase.
insights.quote: integrate conduct improvement and discipline enforcement with anti-corruption measures
insights.locator: The transformation of anti-corruption into a system of political supervision

insights.claim: Xi's January speech to the CCDI, published in full shortly before the plenum, framed implementing Central Committee decisions as a basic requirement of political discipline and warned that anyone who violates it must be held accountable.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Explicit framing of implementation as political discipline raises the personal cost for officials of deviating from central directives.
insights.quote: We cannot merely shout slogans, still less say one thing and do another. Anyone who violates these requirements must be held accountable.
insights.locator: Xi said in a speech to the CCDI in January
